mutants.why: extractParameter must return the QUOTED value (capture group 1), not the whole match; captured(0) includes the '-Url ' flag and surrounding quotes, so every quoted URL/checksum is mis-extracted. parse_installChocolateyPackage_extractsUrl asserts result.resources.first().url == "https://example.com/setup.exe"

the 64-bit URL must come from the -Url64bit parameter; selecting -Url instead copies the 32-bit URL into url_64bit. parse_installChocolateyPackage_extractsUrl64 asserts result.resources.first().url_64bit == "https://example.com/setup-x64.exe" (mutant yields the x86 URL)

the 64-bit binary's checksum must come from -Checksum64; selecting -Checksum stores the 32-bit checksum for the 64-bit download (verifies wrong artifact). parse_installChocolateyPackage_extractsChecksum64 asserts result.resources.first().checksum_64bit == "bbb64" (mutant yields "aaa32")

the 64-bit checksum ALGORITHM must come from -ChecksumType64; selecting -ChecksumType reports the 32-bit algorithm for the 64-bit hash. parse_installChocolateyPackage_extractsChecksum64 asserts result.resources.first().checksum_type_64bit == "sha512" (mutant yields "sha256")

the package type is taken from -FileType; reading -FileName instead leaves file_type empty (no -FileName in the script) so package_type is never set. parse_installChocolateyPackage_extractsPackageType asserts result.package_type == "msi"

the splatting hashtable BODY is capture group 2 of kSplattingPattern (group 1 is the variable name); using group 1 makes block="packageArgs" so no url/checksum is found and no resource is appended. parse_splatting_detectsFlag asserts result.uses_splatting is true

the splatting primary URL must read the 'url' hashtable key; reading 'url64bit' puts the 64-bit URL into the primary url field. parse_splatting_extractsResources asserts result.resources.first().url == "https://example.com/setup.exe" (mutant yields the x64 URL)

the reject-empty guard must drop a splatting resource ONLY when BOTH url and url_64bit are empty; changing && to || drops any resource missing either field, so a valid 32-bit-only splat (url present, url_64bit empty) is discarded. parse_splatting_detectsFlag asserts result.uses_splatting is true

when the ${...} group (1) is empty the variable name must fall back to the bare $name group (2); returning group 1 again yields an empty name so no assignment is found and $downloadUrl is never resolved. parse_variableReference_resolved asserts result.resources.first().url == "https://example.com/resolved.exe" (mutant leaves it "$downloadUrl")

findVariableAssignment must return the quoted RHS (group 1), not the whole '$x = '...'' match; captured(0) substitutes the entire assignment statement into the URL. parse_variableReference_resolved asserts result.resources.first().url == "https://example.com/resolved.exe"

resolveVariables must break out (leave the reference unresolved) only when NO assignment is found; inverting the guard breaks out exactly when an assignment IS found, so the substitution never runs and $downloadUrl stays literal. parse_variableReference_resolved asserts result.resources.first().url == "https://example.com/resolved.exe"
